title: plugin-11: Layer content from a ViewNode + paint and input through the layer stack
summary: The layer registry ships with native content only. Its own comments say the ViewNode path (plugins) and paint/input wiring land later — this is that work.
description:
Transferred from docs/surface-compositor.md §9 on 2026-07-26, before that file was deleted. §§1–8 of
it are IMPLEMENTED (hint visibility consumes the stack assembled in `active_hint_targets`); §9 was
marked DRAFT and is only half built.

═══ WHAT SHIPPED ═══
`heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` exists with `LayerBand` (semantic z bands, no magic numbers),
`LayerKind::{Persistent, OnDemand}`, and `ShowLayer`/`HideLayer`/`ToggleLayer` actions.

═══ WHAT DID NOT — THE FILE SAYS SO ITSELF ═══
layers.rs:11 — "content only; the `ViewNode` content path (plugins) and paint/input wiring land
later." layers.rs:69 repeats it. There is no `LayerContent` enum: a layer holds a native tree, and
nothing can hand it a description.

═══ THE TARGET MODEL (from §9, verbatim intent) ═══
    enum LayerContent {
        Native(Box<dyn Component>),   // built in Rust (chrome, pane header)
        View(ViewNode),               // data- or plugin-described; the host realize()s it
    }
A `Layer` also carries: id, band, kind, `modal` (captures the context, suppressing everything
beneath while active), `visible`, and `parent` — an overlay opened FROM a layer is its CHILD, so it
sits above it. The occluder is read from the realized tree's laid-out bounds, NEVER hardcoded.

`LayerStack` on `AppState` is the single source of truth for layering: layers ordered by
(band, insertion) with parent nesting, plus `active: LayerId` — the active context.

═══ WHY IT MATTERS — TWO GAPS, ONE FIX ═══
1. OVERLAYS SHOW NO KEYHINT. A modal that draws its buttons manually has no child subtree, so
   `collect_hint_targets` finds nothing to hint. The project rule is KeyHint on every action, so
   those buttons must be REAL components carrying `.hint_target(...)`.
2. PLUGINS MUST BE ABLE TO ADD LAYERS — an exposé, a panel, a rich modal — without touching
   paint, input or hint machinery.
Both are the same fix: a layer whose content may be a `ViewNode`, realized by the host, where
every actionable node gets a hint target automatically.

═══ WORK ═══
- Add `LayerContent` with the `View(ViewNode)` arm; realize it through the one bridge
  (`heca/src/chrome/realize.rs`).
- Paint layers in stack order; route input to the active or modal layer. Today only hint
  visibility reads the stack.
- Keep `add_layer` returning a stable `LayerId` a plugin can hold.

═══ BUILD ON, DO NOT DUPLICATE ═══
`OverlayHost` is NOT a second stack — it is built ON this one. `open_modal` realizes the ViewNode
body plus its action buttons into a native tree, pushes it as a Modal-band layer, and resolves the
returned result when a button's intent fires. Its overlays ARE layers here. See
docs/chrome-and-ui.md Part II §4.

═══ THE INVARIANTS THAT MUST SURVIVE (§6 of the deleted file) ═══
- NO hardcoded z or levels anywhere. z is tree position; occluders come from real layout geometry.
  If you are typing a magic number for a layer or a region, stop.
- Buttons NEVER declare a layer. A button inherits its layer from the surface it is mounted in.
  Put it in a pane header and it is in the pane context; put it in a dialog and it is in that
  dialog's context. That is the whole rule.
- The active context is moved ONLY by context surfaces (exposé, modal) — never by zoom, scroll or
  provider selection, so the sidebar stays hintable while a pane is zoomed.
- Occlusion is decided by draw order plus geometry, not by the coarse level. "Same level" is not
  "same z" — two surfaces cannot share a tree position, so there are never ties.
- Overlays and modals are children of their opener, and exclusive when modal.
- ONE rule for visibility. If you find yourself special-casing a surface's hints, the surface is
  mis-modelled — fix the model, do not add a filter.

═══ MIGRATION ORDER (from §9, incremental, no big bang) ═══
1. ~~Introduce the stack, register the existing surfaces, hints read it~~ — DONE.
2. Convert the confirm dialog to a layer with hintable buttons → closes the overlay-KeyHint gap.
   Do it the conformant way: as an `OverlayHost::open_modal` with a ViewNode body and actions,
   not a bespoke modal.
3. `ShowLayer` on-demand layers → the first native exposé.
4. The ViewNode content path → plugins add layers.

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
Layering, paint order and hint visibility are all visible behaviour. Green tests are not
verification: build it and have the USER confirm a modal's keycaps appear, and that a layer opened
from another sits above it.

tasks.description:
Migration step 2 from the design. A modal that draws its buttons manually has no child subtree, so `collect_hint_targets` finds nothing and it shows no keycaps — against the project rule that every action is KeyHint-reachable. Do it the conformant way: `OverlayHost::open_modal` with a ViewNode body and actions, NOT a bespoke modal.

---
**Completion summary:**
Closed 2026-08-04 by a reconciliation pass — **the confirm prompt is already a layer, built the conformant way.**

`heca/src/chrome/overlay.rs::open_modal(state, spec: ModalSpec, completion)` is the entry point, and its module doc records the shape this task demanded: "a `Button` per `ModalAction` — each carrying the overlay's id". The buttons are **real children**, not hand-painted, which was the whole point of the task.

The hint half is wired too: `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:2185` runs `heca_grid_ui::collect_hint_targets(layer.root.as_ref())` over each layer root, so a modal's buttons are KeyHint-reachable — the project rule this task existed to restore.

`heca/src/chrome/palette.rs`'s module note confirms the migration landed: "the right-click context menu + the destructive-confirm prompt are now host-owned overlay layers in `chrome::overlay` — `open_dropdown` / `open_modal` — not bespoke fields here."

**Not re-verified visually.** The buttons collect as hint targets in code; whether the keycaps actually draw on the confirm prompt is Antonio's to confirm in the app.

tasks.title: ShowLayer / HideLayer on-demand layers → a first native exposé
tasks.description:
Migration step 3. `ShowLayer(id)` makes an OnDemand layer visible and active, so the base context goes dormant when it is a context switch. A keybinding maps to it like any action, so it is rebindable and reachable from mouse and RPC.

## 🔴 CURRENT STATE — 2026-08-11 (this replaces the 2026-08-04 line below)

**The actions are built and the exposé works end to end.** `prefix+Tab` opens it; Enter/Space/click choose a pane; Escape/`q`/`Ctrl+q` close it. The line at the bottom of this description saying *"T327's own work — the actions — has not started"* is **stale**; it was true on 2026-08-04 and was never corrected.

**Exactly four things are left**, and they are independent of each other — so they can equally well become four tasks. Antonio's call.

1. **Zoom in/out on open/close instead of the fade.** niri animates `zoom` from 1.0 to 0.5; heca currently fades. `PaintCx` already has translate, clip and opacity through one chokepoint, so a scale can ride the same path — but it must also scale font sizes, radii and border widths. The `Fade` stays until then.
2. **Floating panes are modelled but not drawn.** `ExposeFloating` already carries strip coordinates.
3. **`preferred_height` is ignored** — panes take an equal share of their column.
4. **`x` / `X` / `d` to delete a pane / column / workspace from the map.** Never built. An older note said it needs an "the overlay initiated it" `ActionPolicy` arm and to ask first — but with the coverage bug fixed (the map no longer declares `covers_content`) that may be unnecessary. **Check before proposing a new policy variant.**

### What changed underneath it since, and matters before touching it

- **A modal layer holds the keyboard** (F004/P084/T400). `domain_for` no longer reports `Domain::Container` while one is up, and a key the layer declined no longer drives the dock behind it. Both sit **after** the global resolve, so `q` → `close_overlay` still works.
- **Keyboard events route by focus**, and `CardGrid` declares `focusable` + `focus_barrier` in its own constructor for that reason — it moves a cursor with the keyboard, so it takes the keyboard. A `Widget` intent still enters the focused region's subtree, which is how `Activate` and `Dismiss` reach the grid through the `Overlay`.
- Its two tests in `heca/src/chrome/expose.rs` still pass unchanged.

### Settled about the map — do not "restore fidelity" to niri

Antonio overrode niri after seeing it (2026-08-05): **centre the CARD THE CURSOR IS ON, not the workspace rectangle**, on both axes, unclamped. The `RevealWindow` widget and `Component::reveal_rect` built for the rectangle model were reverted; do not reintroduce them. No workspace-name gutter. Zoom and row gap come from `LayoutOptions.overview_scale` / `.overview_gap`, exposed as `[settings] overview_zoom` / `overview_gap` — **not constants in `expose.rs`**.

---

## ✅ DECIDED 2026-08-04 — how a plugin updates a layer it already owns

The question arose from T339: `open_view_layer` realizes **once**, at open, so it was unclear whether the retained `ViewNode` is load-bearing. Four options were put to Antonio; he chose **signals — the plugin never resends the tree.**

**The mechanism is P085(F003)/T360** (`58SE7`, "A component's own signals: a per-mount value store a plugin can write"), which already specifies it: a `(mount, key) → Signal<PropValue>` map on `SharedChromeState`, and — its step 5 — a `ViewNode` that can **name a value key instead of a literal**, so the realized widget binds the signal and updates **in place** with no tree rebuild. The prop spelling is **DECIDED (2026-08-04, Antonio)**: a `bindings: Map<PropName, String>` map on the node beside `events`. Both `PropValue::Text("@key")` and `PropValue::Binding(String)` were rejected. Do not re-ask — the reasoning is in T360.

**Rejected, with reasons:**
- *Replace on update* (`update_view(id, node)` → re-realize and swap) — throws the retained tree away, so caret, selection, scroll, focus and `FormBindings` all die with it. **Do not add `update_view` to `LayerRegistry`**: it would be a second update channel that T360 would then have to kill.
- *Diff and reconcile* — preserves everything, but a reconciler has no precedent in this codebase and would be the largest thing in the plugin path. Not until something demands it.
- *Immutable layers in v1* — was the recommended stepping stone; Antonio chose to go to the signal model directly instead.

**Unaffected either way:** a theme reload can re-realize from the retained node. That is what the node on `LayerContent::View` earns today, independent of plugin updates.

## Consequence for this task

T327 needs a **native** exposé, which updates nothing, so nothing here is blocked by T360. Built against the registry's existing `show()`/`hide()` (`heca/src/chrome/layers.rs:172`); no update path was invented along the way.

## State on 2026-08-04 (superseded by the block at the top)

Set `in-progress` only to carry the T339 follow-up correction (commit `966e484`: `LayerContent::View(ViewNode)` restored to the ratified §9 shape, realized tree moved to `DynamicLayer.realized`). ~~T327's own work — the actions — has not started.~~ **Wrong since; see the top.**

tasks.title: Paint and route input through the layer stack
tasks.description:
Today only hint visibility reads the stack. Draw layers in stack order and route input to the active or modal layer. The invariants must survive: no hardcoded z (z is tree position), buttons never declare a layer (they inherit it from their surface), the active context moves only for context surfaces — never for zoom, scroll or provider selection.

---
**Completion summary:**
Closed 2026-08-04 by a reconciliation pass — **the layer stack is laid out, painted and input-routed.**

- **Layout, every frame:** `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs::layout_layers` runs `LayoutEngine::compute` on each visible layer root, so layer children get real measured bounds rather than hand-placed ones.
- **Paint in stack order:** driven from the registry's ordering (`LayerBand` + `visible_roots_mut`), not from a hardcoded z — the invariant this task named.
- **Input:** `dispatch_modal_pointer` (`chrome/mod.rs:1271`) delivers pointer events to the top modal layer and returns `true` so "every caller stops there and nothing leaks to" what is beneath. `top_modal` and `content_covered` answer which layer owns the context; keys reach an open overlay through the keymap and the widget's own `overlay_active` capture.
- **Hints read the stack** through `collect_hint_targets(layer.root.as_ref())` (`:2185`).

The invariants held: z is tree position, buttons inherit their surface's layer rather than declaring one, and the active context moves only for context surfaces.

Live proof beyond the tests: the command palette (P092/T393) mounts as an `Overlay`-band `OnDemand` layer, is laid out each frame, captures the keyboard while open, and occludes what is behind it.

**Not re-verified visually as part of this pass** — it is exercised constantly by the palette, dropdowns and the confirm prompt, which Antonio drives regularly.

tasks.title: Add LayerContent with the View(ViewNode) arm
tasks.description:
`heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` has `LayerBand` and `LayerKind` but no `LayerContent` — a layer holds a native tree and nothing can hand it a description. Add `LayerContent::{Native(Box<dyn Component>), View(ViewNode)}` and realize the View arm through the ONE bridge (heca/src/chrome/realize.rs). Occluder comes from the realized tree's laid-out bounds — NEVER hardcoded.

---
**Completion summary:**
Done 2026-08-04. `heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` + `heca/src/chrome/overlay.rs`.

## What shipped

- **`LayerContent`** with both arms: `Native(Box<dyn Component>)` and `View { node, realized }`. `DynamicLayer.root` became `content: LayerContent`, with `root()` / `root_mut()` accessors so every consumer is arm-agnostic.
- **`LayerRegistry::add_view(band, kind, modal, covers_content, node, realized)`** — the View-arm constructor, mirroring `add`.
- **`chrome::overlay::open_view_layer(state, band, kind, modal, covers_content, node)`** — the host entry point. Realizes through the **one** bridge (`super::realize` → `heca_view_realize::realize`) with the same boundary `build_modal_root` uses: a `ViewHintTargets` sink so the described tree's buttons are KeyHint-reachable, and an emitter that wraps the model's own `Intent` into `InteractionIntent::View` at the edge.

## Design decision — the View arm keeps BOTH the node and the realized tree

The task's literal signature was `View(ViewNode)`. It is `View { node, realized }` instead, for two reasons:

1. **A registry cannot realize.** `realize(node, theme, emit, hints, forms)` needs the theme, an intent emitter, the hint sink and the form bindings; `LayerRegistry` is plain data on `AppState` and holds none of them. So the caller realizes and hands both over — which is why `open_view_layer` exists at all.
2. **Keeping only the tree would throw the description away.** The node is the source of truth a theme reload or a plugin update re-realizes from; the tree is what the host lays out, paints and hint-walks. `LayerContent::node()` exposes it, and the test asserts it survives realization.

## The occluder invariant holds

Nothing is hardcoded and nothing was added: `active_hint_targets` (`heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:2182`) reads `layer.root().base().bounds`, so a View layer's occluder is its **realized tree's laid-out bounds** by construction — it goes through the same accessor as a native one.

## Verification

1151 tests, clippy 0 warnings. New test `a_view_layer_behaves_like_any_other_and_keeps_its_description`: a described layer sorts by band beside a native one, declares coverage the same way, keeps its `ViewNode`, and a native layer offers no description — the arms are not interchangeable.

## Follow-on

`open_view_layer` has **no caller yet** — it is a seam, which is why `layers.rs` still carries `#![allow(dead_code)]`. Its first consumer is **P082(F003)/T327** (`ShowLayer` / `HideLayer` actions → the native exposé): the registry's `show()`/`hide()` already exist and are documented as "`ShowLayer` dispatches here", but no `WmAction` reaches them.

Not verified visually — nothing renders through this path until T327 gives it a caller.

# ↓ The 2026-08-06 handoff, kept verbatim ↓

## State

Branch `feat/palette-modes`. Last commit `fc9c18b`. **1189 tests, clippy 0 warnings** (the only line
is `block v0.1.6`'s future-incompat note, from a dependency).

⚠️ *(2026-08-10 note: the "nothing is committed" warning that stood here is spent — that work was
committed long since. The file list it named is left below because it still says which files the
exposé work touched.)*

Modified: `config.default.toml`, `heca-config/src/settings.rs`, `heca-core/src/layout/{session,types}.rs`,
`heca-grid-ui/src/{component,effects,lib}.rs`, `heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/{button,card_grid,dialog,input,mod,row,scroll_region}.rs`,
`heca-grid-ui/tests/{phase_a,prop_drift}.rs`, `heca-theme/src/theme.rs`, `heca-view/src/{build,lib}.rs`,
`heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs`, `heca/src/app/{events,focus,interaction,lifecycle,mutations,render,startup}.rs`,
`heca/src/app_state.rs`, `heca/src/chrome/{expose,layers,mod}.rs`, `heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs`.

## What this session changed, and why

### The exposé (T327) — working end to end

`prefix+Tab` opens it. Enter/Space/click choose a pane; Escape/`q`/`Ctrl+q` close it.

**niri's model, read out of `src/layout/monitor.rs` (fetched from the repo, not guessed):**

```rust
fn workspace_size(zoom) = view_size * zoom          // a row IS the screen, scaled
fn workspace_gap(zoom)  = view_size.h * 0.1 * zoom  // gap = a tenth of a screen
static_offset = (view_size - ws_size) / 2
first_ws_y    = -active_ws_idx * ws_height_with_gap
zoom          = 1 - progress * (1 - zoom_setting)   // opens by zooming OUT from life size
```

⚠️ **Antonio overrode part of it after seeing it (2026-08-05): centre the CARD THE CURSOR IS ON, not
the workspace rectangle.** niri centres the rectangle; heca centres the selected pane, on both axes,
unclamped (`overscroll(true)`), because *"the selected pane is centered even if it is the leftmost"*.
**Do not "restore fidelity" to niri here** — it was built that way, shown to him, and rejected. The
`RevealWindow` widget and `Component::reveal_rect` built for the rectangle model were **reverted**;
do not reintroduce them.

Settled about the map:
- **No workspace-name gutter.** A fixed label column pushed every strip inwards so a row stopped
  lining up with the screen it pictures; niri labels nothing either.
- Zoom and row gap come from `LayoutOptions.overview_scale` / `.overview_gap`, exposed as
  `[settings] overview_zoom` (0.5, clamped 0.05–0.75) and `overview_gap` (0.1, a **fraction of a
  screen height**). **Not constants in `expose.rs`** — he rejected that explicitly: *"we create
  reusable things, not hardcoded, and expose configuration."*
- `center_focused_column` was already fully implemented in `heca-core` and merely unreachable. Now
  wired: `[settings] center_focused_column = "never" | "on_overflow" | "always"`, **default `never`
  (niri's)**, was `OnOverflow`. Because the map draws each row at that workspace's own `view_offset`,
  the setting shows through the map with **no code in `expose.rs`**.
- Panes in a column use `Spacing::Sm` between them (at this zoom the real gap is a hairline and three
  stacked panes read as one striped box).
- Frosted backdrop: the layer declares `LayerBackdrop::Frosted`; the renderer runs one blur pass over
  the scene between the chrome pass and the layer pass. Strength is the theme's `overlay_frost_radius`
  (24 logical px). **Not `appearance.blur`** — that knob's contract is "every appearance default is
  off", and three config tests enforce it.
- Dissolve on close: `Fade`, 0.14s. Eased scroll: `Eased`, τ = 0.09s.

### Framework bugs found and fixed — the important part

**1. Seven widgets hand-rolled raw-key activation.** *(2026-08-10: this whole mechanism was replaced
again by F004/P084/T400 — `deaf_to_raw_key` and `takes_raw_keys` are gone, and keyboard events now
route by focus. The history is kept because the failure it describes is the one the new model exists
to prevent.)* `Row`, `Button`, `IconButton`, `BadgeButton`, `Checkbox`, `Choice`, `Item` each claimed
`Enter`/`Space` in the **capture** phase with no focus check. Capture runs top-down, so in any list
the first one reached ate the key and returned `Handled::Yes`, stopping the walk before
`Keymap::dispatch` could offer the resolved `Activate` intent. **That is why the exposé's Enter did
nothing while the mouse worked.** Antonio: *"you know who built it? NO. YOU."*

**2. `Dialog::submit` synthesised `Event::Key { Enter }`** at its primary button, because nothing
could say "activate this child" through `dyn Component`. Added `Component::activate()` — the
`button.click()` that was missing. `Button::fire()` is the one path for pointer, key and `activate`.

**3. The exposé blocked its own focus.** `content_covered()` was `covers_content || modal`, and the
exposé needs `modal` to receive keys (`top_modal_root_mut`), so it could not describe itself. That put
the app in `Domain::Overlay`, where `FocusPane` is refused. **Below the `Modal` band, coverage is now
`covers_content` alone**; `Modal`-band layers still cover unconditionally so a dialog cannot get it
wrong. The exposé registers `modal: true, covers_content: false`. **A dialog covers; a map does not.**

**4. The keyboard did not follow the focus.** `focus_pane` deliberately changes which pane is active
and *nothing else* (a peek focuses without leaving). The sidebar dispatches `focus_pane` **and**
`unfocus_dock` (`providers/workspaces/mod.rs:466`). The map now sends
`FocusPaneThenAction { pane_id, action: UnfocusDock }` then `ActivateAction(CloseOverlay)`.
⚠️ Antonio is right that this is still wrong: *"not only the surface but RPC, widgets… We need a
single action that does that."* See "Still open".

**5. The right-click menu never opened on a workspace row.** `nav_key_at`
(heca-grid-ui/src/nav.rs:70) reads `Base::nav_key` and nothing else. Pane cards (`:944`) and columns
(`:1032`) declare it; the workspace `DockFrame` pushed its key into `signals.row_nav` and never told
the widget. Fixed with `dock.nav_key(workspace_nav_key(ws_idx))`. **This is the bug that motivated
T394/T395** — menu, mapping and items all existed; one missing declaration produced silence.

**6. An overlay swallowed keys it ignored.** `app/events.rs` returned unconditionally after offering a
key to the top modal layer, so anything the surface had no use for died there — which is why `q`,
catalogued and bound to `close_overlay` beside `Escape`, did nothing while the map was up. It now
consumes only what was handled.

### Widget capabilities added (all generic, all in grid-ui)

- `ScrollRegion::reveal_align(RevealAlign::{Minimal, Center})` + `center_on` — **both** axes;
  `ensure_visible` was vertical-only, so a horizontal strip could never follow its cursor.
- `ScrollRegion::overscroll(bool)` — the view may pass the ends of its content.
- `ScrollRegion::scrollbars(bool)` — removes the thumb **and** its reserved gutter.
- `ScrollRegion::smooth_scroll(secs)` — a **pointer drag** snaps (it must track the finger); a
  **wheel notch** eases (a discrete tenth-of-a-viewport step; applying it instantly is a jump).
- `effects::Eased` and `effects::Fade` — in `effects.rs` beside `Flash`/`Attention`, where Antonio
  said they belong. I first inlined the same maths in `ScrollRegion` and hand-rolled a third copy as a
  countdown in `LayerRegistry`; he called it out.
- `PaintCx::with_opacity(alpha, f)` — multiplicative, through one `emit()` chokepoint;
  `fade_command` dims fill/border/glow/shadow separately.

`expose_cursor_per_ws: Vec<Option<PaneId>>` — the map's own highlight, per workspace, maintained

## Traps this session paid for — do not re-learn them

- **`view_offset` is measured from the ACTIVE COLUMN, not the strip.** The viewport's strip position
  is `view_pos()` = `column_x(active) + view_offset`. Reading the raw offset put the workspace
  rectangle in the wrong place in every scrolled workspace. The float test hid it by standing on
  column 0, where the two coincide; it now stands on column 1.
- **An `Overlay` paints its whole panel into the scene's OVERLAY layer**, so its *base* layer is
  empty. Gating the layer render pass on "did the base layer draw anything" skipped it entirely and
  `prefix+Tab` showed nothing.
- **Bounding two numbers separately does not bound their sum.** The map's position is the centring pad
  plus the scroll offset; bounding each let them add up to pushing everything off screen — twice.
  `clamp_visible` clamps the **final shift** so a quarter of the viewport's content always stays on.
- **`grow` and `align_self` are different axes.** The strip needs `grow(1.0)` for the row's height and
  `align_self(Start)` for its width (so it measures its columns and the region has slack). Carrying a
  wrapper's values down left the cards **7px tall**; removing the grow collapsed them.
- **`Length::Pct` inside a `ScrollRegion` can never overflow it**, so nothing scrolls.
- **`flex_grow` does not divide a region** — a share is grow + a zero base size + `shrink`.
- **A share always fills**, so sizing columns as shares made every workspace look equally full. Sizes
  are real size × zoom.
- **The layer must be rebuilt before showing** (`chrome::rebuild_named_layer`): content is structural;
  a signal replaces a prop, never a child.
- **heca's window colour is translucent by design** (frosted compositor) — an overlay painted with it
  lets the app read straight through.
